title: Alice & Bob Tests GPU Decoding for Cat-Qubit Error Correction with NVIDIA NVQLink
source_used: Alice & Bob press release (alice-bob.com, 13 Oct 2026); HPCwire page blocked (403); Scientific Computing World teaser matches
key_facts: Alice & Bob, a quantum computing company based in Paris and Boston, said on 13 Oct 2026 it implemented GPU decoding of its LDPC-cat error-correction codes using Nvidia's NVQLink.
It was a proof of concept using synthetic data; the company says it is the first time LDPC-cat codes have been decoded on GPUs through NVQLink.
The company says it is not real-time decoding, but the results show decoding can scale as several error signals (syndromes) are decoded in parallel.

The test used an NVQLink connection with Quantum Machines' OPX1000 controller and Open Acceleration Stack, which has microsecond-scale round-trip latency, and checked whether measurement data could move from the control electronics to the GPU.
Next, Alice & Bob will optimise the data pipeline to reach the speed needed for real-time decoding.
Juliette Peyronnet, US general manager of Alice & Bob, said the next step is making decoding fast enough to keep pace with the quantum computer.
Sam Stanwyck, director of quantum product at Nvidia, said the work shows NVQLink can accelerate the real-time decoding needed for fault-tolerant machines.
In March 2026 the companies reported a 1 hour 57 minute runtime for decoding simulated data of Alice & Bob's Elevator Codes with Nvidia's CUDA-Q platform.
quote_evidence: The proof of concept using synthetic data is the first time LDPC-cat codes have been decoded on GPUs via the low-latency, high throughput NVQLink architecture, and moves the company a step closer to fast, scalable error correction for its cat-qubit quantum computers.
Though a proof of concept and not constituting real-time decoding, the results show how decoding can scale by becoming more efficient as several syndromes are decoded in parallel.
Alice & Bob will now optimize the pipeline, the chain of steps that carry the measurement data through NVQLink to the GPU, to enable the performance needed for real-time decoding.
why_it_matters_hint: Fast classical decoding is one of the hard parts of error-corrected quantum computing, and this shows a first step on Nvidia GPUs.
